correctness.rationale: For all positive a,b,c,d, the case proof accounts for every contiguous factor through four run types. Unary factors fix run dominance, 10 and 01 fix boundary requirements, and the two longer extremal 01 factors yield the remaining middle-pair inequalities. The three disjoint position families yield exact N2 and the phase, with explicit cardinality-three witnesses ensuring upper bound. Independent occurrence-mask and direct factor-set finite checkers agree on 1296 and 256 parameter tuples respectively; finite tests are not asserted as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary full texts give generic methods, word-operation bounds and special-sequence classifications; the exact all-positive-four-run witness classification, count and phase are not covered by their inspected results. Public indexed results on fixed-length censuses or periodic special cases cannot imply the general four-parameter theorem. Search is not a universal novelty proof; unindexed coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-four-run theorem may occur under different terminology in literature not indexed or not read completely.
Indexed special cases and generic algorithms do not establish independent priority for the elementary factor lemmas.

value.rationale: The four-run family is the first binary alternating run class exhibiting both optimal sizes 2 and 3. The result determines for every positive run-length quadruple which size occurs and enumerates every size-two witness, including non-monotone one-unit exceptional regions. This is a complete natural class result for a compression-linked invariant, not a fixed numerical slice or routine estimate; it does not determine size-three multiplicities.
